review_method: Read official product documentation, institutional service documentation, GitHub repository metadata, READMEs, and the named StingChat commit. No candidate was installed or run.
version_note: LibreChat documentation was labeled Latest (dev). The releases collection listed v0.8.9-rc1, published 2026-10-26, and v0.8.8, published 2026-10-01; both were marked prerelease by GitHub. Pin and verify a release before implementation. Documentation is evidence of capability, not a test of a deployment.

sources.name: LibreChat
sources.finding: Chat, agents, tools, file context, and exports provide the base. Configure approved capabilities instead of rebuilding the chat harness.
sources.reuse: Retain the conversation UI and agent/tool runtime.
sources.limit: This deliverable is a concept prototype, not a running LibreChat fork.

sources.name: LibreChat access controls and balances
sources.finding: Roles, groups, resource access, and account credit balances cover much of institution management.
sources.reuse: Configure school profiles and approved helpers; use upstream balances for account allowances.
sources.limit: The balance reference describes application-wide defaults. Do not claim a new course-budget system or assume every latest-doc feature is in a chosen release.

sources.name: LibreChat Admin Panel
sources.finding: A separate management UI covers users, groups, roles, and configuration overrides.
sources.reuse: Evaluate and adapt the existing panel rather than build a second administration stack.
sources.limit: Preview maturity and compatibility require evaluation. This application has a separate license.

sources.name: LibreChat SharePoint / OneDrive picker
sources.finding: Select Microsoft 365 files and attach them to a conversation using Entra-based access.
sources.reuse: Keep this file-context path in the pilot.
sources.limit: Read/attach functionality, not shared task folders, live document editing, or file write-back. Requires tenant configuration.

sources.name: bruchris/canvas-lms-mcp
sources.finding: Implements Canvas tools and an OAuth-brokered multi-user connection profile.
sources.reuse: Evaluate a narrow set of course, assignment, page, and rubric reads for LibreChat.
sources.limit: The connector also exposes broad teaching/admin operations. Enforce the pilot allowlist and per-user access on the server; hiding tools or adding prompt instructions is insufficient. Compatibility and permissions remain untested here.

sources.name: vishalsachdev/canvas-mcp
sources.finding: Provides student and educator Canvas workflows, including tools far beyond selected course-context reads.
sources.reuse: Compare its read tools and client support with the other candidate.
sources.limit: No connector has been selected or validated for the school. Raw tool counts and repository activity are not evidence of suitability.

sources.name: StingChat
sources.finding: The June 30, 2025 commit adds teacher-tool forms for lessons, quizzes, rubrics, worksheets, and IEPs.
sources.reuse: Reference the idea of guided teacher prompts; favor a few ordinary saved helpers in the new scope.
sources.limit: Repository last push: 2025-07-07. README largely inherits upstream content. No school deployment, maintenance readiness, or security properties were established. No code was copied.

sources.name: AISAchat
sources.finding: Repository describes LibreChat for the University of Oregon AI Student Association.
sources.reuse: A precedent for small institutional customization.
sources.limit: Last push: 2024-04-24. Reviewed README and recent commit metadata show configuration changes; no substantial current education platform was verified.

sources.name: Stanford AI Playground
sources.finding: University IT identifies LibreChat as its foundation and documents institutional eligibility and access.
sources.reuse: Reference institution-provided access with a familiar general-purpose chat interface.
sources.limit: An operational precedent, not a separately verified reusable school fork.

sources.name: Brown CCV LibreChat
sources.finding: Brown documents university sign-in, model selection, file attachments, and monthly account credits.
sources.reuse: Reference simple institution-funded access and a visible allowance.
sources.limit: University deployment practices do not establish K–12 suitability or transferable privacy guarantees.

assessment: Substantial pieces exist already. The useful new work is a school configuration, a selected-context Canvas experience, a small set of education-specific helpers, and clear student-facing guidance. The reviewed sources do not establish a complete, maintained, turnkey high-school edition.
scope_boundary: No LMS replacement, grading/submission workflow, shared-folder agent orchestration, live document editor, or multi-agent work board in the pilot. Preserve those earlier ideas in the archive.
